summary.headline: JD Cables H2 FY26 revenue (total income) rose 70% to INR243 crores; FY26 EBITDA INR48.11 crores, PAT INR31.72 crores, order book INR515 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 total income reached INR365 crores (up 45.67% YoY), with EBITDA of INR48.11 crores (up 40%) and PAT of INR31.72 crores (up 44%). H2 total income was INR243 crores, up 70% against H1-equivalent FY25 turnover of INR143 crores, with H2 EBITDA of INR28 crores (up 52%) and PAT of INR19 crores (up 69%). Management is guiding to 50-60% revenue growth in FY27 and a new Jamshedpur capacity coming online, while the EPC business entry is adding working capital strain. Analyst questions focused on negative operating cash flow, the H1-to-H2 margin drop, and the split between EPC and cable revenue.

financial_highlights.value: Analyst cited ~15% in H1 falling to ~12% in H2; management did not dispute the figures
financial_highlights.change: Management said margins were broadly similar YoY

financial_highlights.value: Negative, cited as about INR70 crores by one analyst and INR74 crores by another; not confirmed by management

segments.name: Cables and conductors (core manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about 28,000 km per annum (Unit I 6,000 km, Unit II 22,000 km); products include power, control, instrumentation and service cables and AAC, AAAC, ACSR conductors. Management expects 30-40% growth in this segment in FY27. Cables and wires were about 76% of FY26 revenue per an analyst question.

segments.name: EPC / infrastructure
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC revenue about INR30 crores; FY27 expected minimum INR200 crores. Around 10% of the National Highway (NHDP Phase 5, Bihar-Jharkhand border) EPC project is complete. Management cited about 8% margin, later clarified as PAT margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 50-60%, and similar again in FY28, per management.
EBITDA margin expected at 12-13%, similar to current levels; management confirmed a double-digit EBITDA target for FY27.
EPC revenue target minimum INR200 crores in FY27 against INR30 crores in FY26; the full EPC project is expected to be substantially executed by FY27 end.
Order book target of INR700-800 crores by 31 March 2027, per management's conservative view.
Capex planned at about INR20-30 crores, depending on order flow; advance payments already made for land adjacent to the new plant.

New Jamshedpur (Dankuni) facility of about 1.18 lakh sq ft: conductor division awaiting power connection, cable division expected within about two months; full utilisation of new capacity expected in FY27 at 70-80%.
capex_capacity: New industrial facility of about 1.18 lakh sq ft acquired (Jamshedpur, also referred to as Dankuni in the Q&A); conductor division equipment installed, awaiting electricity connection expected in June 2026.
Cable division expected to start within about two months; management expects operations at a good pace by September 2026.
Management says capacity can double in Phase 1 and reach 3-4x within two years, subject to orders.
New product lines added: MVCC, AL-59 conductors, HTLS conductors and HE cables; BIS licences needed before full-scale sales, timing uncertain.
Capex of about INR20-30 crores planned for FY27, contingent on order levels.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR515 crores at 31 March 2026, with a timeline of about 1.5 years; split per management about INR300 crores EPC and INR200 crores cables and conductors (mixed).

Tenders of more than INR1,000 crores bid across EPC and cable/transmission-distribution, with results pending; management said it lacks prior track record in T&D tenders, so no conversion ratio was given.
Non-order book (repeat and short-cycle) revenue cited qualitatively; management did not provide a FY26 split.
West Bengal seen as an opportunity after the state government change; management said orders had not yet been received as of the call, pending cabinet and portfolio allocation.
Competitive intensity and pricing were not discussed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from H1 to H2, and what margin range should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to higher expenses and bulk supply, called it marginal, and guided to similar margins going forward, confirming 12-13% when asked.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash burn is there, and how will working capital be funded in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital build is from EPC execution and growth, with bills deducted at once; it expects to use bank debt, says banks are willing to lend, and cited sufficient cash and bank balance. No specific debt quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: What EPC revenue and margin are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EPC revenue about INR30 crores; FY27 minimum INR200 crores. EPC margin around 8%, which management later said was PAT margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products deliver double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins better than existing products and said it expects double-digit, without a firm number until sales begin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR4 crores to INR24 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to EPC startup expenses, with related invoices still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is infrastructure/EPC a recurring business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it will be recurring, and that EPC is forward integration because electrification works need cables and conductors.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in FY26 (analysts cited about INR70-74 crores) and rising inventory and receivable days, with working capital cycle of about 110-120 days cited by an analyst; management did not give a figure.
Rising debt: management expects bank borrowing to fund working capital and EPC, with no quantum disclosed.
Margin visibility: management cited similar margins but gave no segment-level margin guidance for EPC versus cables; the EPC margin was ambiguous between EBITDA and PAT.
Commissioning delays: power connection for the conductor division is still pending, and BIS licences for new products may delay full utilisation.
Tender conversion: about INR1,000 crores bid with no conversion ratio given and no prior T&D tender experience.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity, with forward targets (50-60% revenue growth, 3-4x capacity) stated firmly. Vague or evasive on cash flow, tender conversion, the EPC margin definition and the non-order book split, deferring to later disclosure. Several answers were given as "we are expecting" without quantification.
